title: $120,000 in a Gift Bag: The Juror Who Called the Police

lines.say: A hundred and twenty thousand dollars in cash, in a Hallmark gift bag, left at a juror's door in the first Feeding Our Future fraud trial.
lines.show: $120,000 in cash, in a Hallmark gift bag, left at a juror's door in the first Feeding Our Future fraud trial.

lines.say: A present, the courier told her stepfather. More, if she voted not guilty.
lines.show: A "present," the courier told her stepfather. More, if she voted not guilty.

scene.src: Gov't sentencing memo, Abdiaziz Farah (D. Minn. 24-cr-173, Dkt. 216)

lines.say: They picked Juror fifty-two, prosecutors say, because they thought she was the youngest juror.
lines.show: They picked Juror 52, prosecutors say, because they thought she was the youngest juror.

scene.src: USAO D. Minn. press release, Jun 26, 2024

lines.say: She called the police that night. All five people behind the plot pleaded guilty, and got four to ten years.
lines.show: She called the police that night. All five people behind the plot pleaded guilty, and got 4 to 10 years.

scene.sub: Bribery of a juror · Feeding Our Future trial

lines.say: Would you have picked up the phone?
